LESSON: READING 4.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 4.2.2 Comprehension under Strand 4. It is aligned with the Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development (KICD) CBC design.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. observe pictures and the title of the text and make predictions on the outcome of the story with peers (low vision) while learners with blindness are guided to read picture descriptions and the title of the text and make predictions on the outcome of the story with peers.

2. read a printed or digital text with appropriate font size and colour contrast related to the theme (low vision) while learners with blindness are guided to read braille or digital text related to the theme.

3. infer the meanings of new words using contextual clues.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. observe pictures and the title of the text and make predictions on the outcome of the story with peers (low vision) while learners with blindness are guided to read picture descriptions and the title of the text and make predictions on the outcome of the story with peers.
2. read a printed or digital text with appropriate font size and colour contrast related to the theme (low vision) while learners with blindness are guided to read braille or digital text related to the theme.
3. infer the meanings of new words using contextual clues.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 4.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
